correctness.rationale: Strict convexity of Euclidean norm squared makes all maximizers of radius R occur at vertices, and u_v strongly exposes v. Consequently -u_v⋅z≥c_v||z|| for z in tangent cone, making S_v a bounded full (d-1)-dimensional slice. For chord deficit δ=ε/2, near each extremal u_v, support inequality bounds angular distance O(δ), while gnomonic U=(u_v+(δ/R)w)/sqrt(1+(δ/R)^2||w||²) turns active facet inequalities into S_v plus thickness O(δ) slabs. Spherical Jacobian contributes (δ/R)^(d-1)(1+O(δ²)); summing disjoint vertex neighborhoods gives stated coefficient and O(ε^d). For orthotope tangent-simplex Gram determinant yields R^d/((d-1)!prod a_i) per vertex, hence 2R/((d-1)!σ_(d-1)prod a_i); for cross-polytope sections are l1 unit balls yielding 2d/((d-1)!σ). Independently derived planar diamond direction-tail slope 2/π and rectangular scaling; no smooth-body conclusion. Finite checks are not universal proof.
